facts.statement: Ordinary24/adaptive64 kernel calls have13-entry UINT64 block-table and slot-output pointer arrays. These are address arrays; their typed output is not a 13-element logical slot vector or measured slot-write byte count.

BlockTable gate requires more than one active group and dcp_world_size==1 for every active group. Fused path also requires no compressed positions/request-index lists. Pointer arrays own distinct group tables/output addresses plus group strides/block sizes/circular flags; max output extent comes from first active table. Fallback per-group/Mamba/compressed branches are separate.

Existing implementation already fuses groups in one launch and selects ordinary versus adaptive request tiles. Tile starts from capped1024, uses power-of-two average request length with minimum16; ordinary parallel tiles cap4 with special1/2-request policy. Adaptive runs one group/request program and chooses small tile versus1024 by actual request length. These are existing behavior, not new optimization gains.

Both kernels reserve a program per group to write PAD_ID through [num_tokens,max_num_tokens). Active rows load QSL/positions, cast positionsINT32, compute group-specific block page/remainder, gather block numbers through a window, then write INT32 slot IDs to dereferenced group buffers. Circular groups force page0 and negative positions to PAD_ID.

Block numbers are loaded asINT32, converted toFP32 for tl.gather, then converted backINT32 before block_size multiplication. Direct integer lookup must preserve baseline rounding or prove representable IDs. Window sizing assumes appropriate page-span/address bounds; no unsupported layout change or current bug is inferred.

Adaptive helper has generic CP mapping, but its selected fused callers pass TOTAL_CP_WORLD_SIZE=1. CP>1 fallback mapping is not established by the selected fused ancestry and must retain its separate interleave/rank ownership domain.

Padded-input kernel72calls already emits both rejection count and selector from cumulative draft counts,INT64 valid counts,QSL. It does not compact rejected queries: original token arange,QSL,positions,slot mapping and sequence-length banks pass through; both CPU sequence-length mirrors are retained. The no-blocking-CPU comment does not make CPU shape/item work an NPU synchronization.

Previous-batch correction gathers valid count,old computed state,previous draft count at max(prev_position,0), then uses participating=(prev_position>=0)&(previous_draft>0). It commits computed prefix and accepted counts only after these gather temporaries exist. A naive in-place fused row update can race with other old-row readers.

Normal worker position path derives int64(computed[req_indices])+query_pos; seq_len=computed+scheduled and tail fill0. Existing CP rebuild/positions-ready alternatives bypass the normal position expression and cannot be silently replaced by it.

Input-ID packing waits pending PP receive, preserves no-prev normal CPU input/optional embeds upload, current→previous row map,new/prefill rows,optional is_token_ids refresh,existing contiguous no-spec fastpath,live sampled IDs and flattened draft IDs. General path constructs four index arrays and scatters sampled before draft IDs withINT32 conversion.

Draft metadata performs consecutive input_ids[logits_indices] then that temporary[target_logits_indices+1]. On valid baseline index domains and stable input/indices, compose the row indices to avoid the intermediate gathered ID vector. Preserve dtype/order/bounds/error domain; count all checks/launch savings only after measurement.

Actual pointer/content equality across groups,old-state alias epochs,tail first/last readers,critical-path/physical traffic andnew tiling cost are not proved by these profiles. They are explicit conditions of the scoped opportunities, not automatic demands for implementing a kernel before recording analysis.
